title: Anand and Kramnik: what the numbers show
outcomes: Quotes a measured habit together with its sample size
States what a count from a game sample does not show
Names what would have to be checked before calling a habit a style

steps.text: **What this lesson claims, and what it does not.** It compares two world champions on a few counted measures, taken from games in our own data: both players rated 2400+, standard games, de-duplicated (The Week in Chess and Lichess broadcasts). It does *not* say who played better, and it gives no verdict on style. A number shows what happened in this sample, nothing more.

**Evidence 1: sample and openings.** Viswanathan Anand: 1,513 games in our data, 1987 to 2026. Vladimir Kramnik: 1,626 games, 2012 to 2025. The windows differ, so the two samples are not the same era. With White, Anand opened 1.e4 in 672 of 762 games (88.2%); Kramnik opened 1.e4 in 277 of 817 (33.9%), 1.Nf3 in 205 (25.1%), 1.d4 in 180 (22.0%) and 1.c4 in 154 (18.8%). Source: our own game data (counts from the games described in the first card).

steps.prompt: The opening shares above are exact for this sample. Say what they do NOT show, for example about why each player chose these moves.

steps.text: **Evidence 2: results and length.** Draws: Anand 794 of 1,513 games (52.5%); Kramnik 553 of 1,626 (34.0%). Average game length: Anand 41.8 moves, Kramnik 47.8 moves. Average opponent rating in the sample: Anand 2729, Kramnik 2663. Draw share depends on opponents, tournament format and the years covered, which differ here. Source: our own game data (counts from the games described in the first card).

**Evidence 3: queens at move 30.** Among games that reached move 30, queens were still on in 689 of 1,233 for Anand (55.9%) and 807 of 1,468 for Kramnik (55.0%). That is a difference of under one percentage point in samples of this size, and we have not tested whether it is meaningful. *Similar here* is the honest reading. Source: our own game data (counts from the games described in the first card).

steps.prompt: Pick the draw share (52.5% against 34.0%) or the game length (41.8 against 47.8 moves). Write what it does not show, and one other measure that could explain it.

steps.text: **Reading a claim like 'X plays in style Y'.** Ask: which sample, how many games, which years, against whom? Is the word defined by a measure (game length, draw share, queens on at move 30)? Did the player choose it, or did opponent and preparation? A count with its sample size is evidence; a style word without a measure is opinion.
